problem:
Use the definition of Laplace transforms to calculate $F(s)=L{f(t)},$ where $f(t)$ is given by 

$$
f(t)={\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t},\, & t\le 2 \\ 2\, & t>2.\end{aligned}
$$

$\,F(s)=L{f(t)}=$ {{field-1}},
valid for {{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
We apply the definition of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =F(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

So, for the piecewise function 

$$
f(t)={\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t},\, & t\le 2 \\ 2\, & t>2\end{aligned}
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{3t}\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{2}^{\infty }2\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{3t-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{2}^{\infty }2{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{(3-s)t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{2}^{\infty }2{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the improper integral diverges if $s\le 0.$

For $s>0,$ we calculate our Laplace transform as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{(3-s)t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{2}^{\infty }2{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{3-s}{[{e}^{(3-s)t}]}_{0}^{2}+{\int }_{2}^{\infty }2{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2(3-s)}-1}{3-s}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{2}^{a}2{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2(3-s)}-1}{3-s}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{(\frac{-2{e}^{-st}}{s})|}_{2}^{a} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2(3-s)}-1}{3-s}-\frac{2}{s}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }({e}^{-as}-{e}^{-2s}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2(3-s)}-1}{3-s}-\frac{2}{s}\cdot (0-{e}^{-2s}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2(3-s)}-1}{3-s}+\frac{2{e}^{-2s}}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>0.$
